answer: Cross-Epoch Action Continuity Rule. Each identity’s action history is hashed into a rolling commitment; a new epoch’s first action must extend the prior thread, and discontinuities trigger a challenge window. Honest agents pay only routine hashing. An attacker must maintain a separate, plausible behavioural river of past actions for every fake identity, since a fresh identity lacking prior history is flagged as a tide shift and rejected. Cost: sustained per-identity record-keeping and action volume across epochs.
